content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Cancellation and Timeouts** as part of **Coroutines, Asynchronous Programming, and Concurrency**. Apply cancellation and timeouts by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Cooperative Cancellation, Cancellation Checks, Timeouts and Cleanup—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous code introduces lifecycle, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Structured concurrency and explicit data flow make these concerns easier to reason about.

items.text: Cooperative Cancellation depends on task lifetime and execution context. Keep child tasks inside an owning scope, handle cancellation cooperatively, and avoid unsynchronized shared mutable state.
